extracted.intended_audience: K-12 and postsecondary school administrators, Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and institutional compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for how recipients (schools, colleges, universities) must respond to reports of Title IX sexual harassment, including reporting channels, standards of promptness and non-deliberate indifference, Title IX Coordinator duties, training and impartiality requirements, grievance process rules, supportive measures, remedies, retaliation prohibitions, and rules about false statements and dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear reporting channels and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department aims to give every complainant and all third parties clear reporting channels (which differ for postsecondary institution students than for elementary and secondary school students). Revised §106.8 states that any person may report sexual harassment (whether or not the person reporting is the person alleged to be the victim) by using the contact information listed for the Title IX Coordinator, which must include an office address, telephone number, and email address; reports may be made at any time, including during non-business hours, by using the telephone number or email address or by mailing to the office address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must list Title IX Coordinator contact info (office address, phone, email) and accept reports at any time and by multiple means (in person, mail, telephone, email). Reporting channels should be clear and predictable; the Department expects recipients to provide these channels for complainants and third-party reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of actual knowledge (elementary/secondary distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised §106.30 defining 'actual knowledge' provides that notice of sexual harassment to any elementary and secondary school employee constitutes actual knowledge to the recipient, and states that 'notice' includes but is not limited to reporting to the Title IX Coordinator as described in §106.8(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For elementary and secondary schools, notice to any employee triggers the recipient's response obligations; the definition of actual knowledge is broader for K-12 than for other contexts. Recipients must be aware how the definition affects prompt-response obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duty to contact complainant about supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised §106.44(a) specifically requires the Title IX Coordinator to contact the complainant to discuss supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes with respect to supportive measures, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator must engage in an interactive discussion with the complainant about available supportive measures, inform them that supportive measures are available with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain how to file a formal complaint. This is a legally binding duty under the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer supportive measures promptly and regardless of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to a complainant; the final regulations make this an explicit part of a recipient's prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response. Supportive measures for complainants may include a different seating assignment or other accommodation so that the complainant does not need to sit next to the respondent in class every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be offered promptly upon notice and irrespective of whether a formal complaint is filed. The requirement recognizes educational institutions' ability to take prompt administrative actions (e.g., leaves, exam accommodations, counseling) to restore or preserve a complainant's equal access to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt response standard — respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised §106.44(a) to require recipients to respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent. The deliberate indifference standard has been tailored for administrative enforcement by adding specific obligations (e.g., offering supportive measures and Title IX Coordinator contact obligations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must act promptly when they have actual knowledge, offering supportive measures and, where applicable, initiating grievance procedures under §106.45 in a reasonably prompt timeframe. Promptness applies both to offering supportive measures and to the overall grievance process (including appeals and informal resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised §106.44(a) requires recipients to treat complainants and respondents equitably by offering supportive measures as defined in §106.30 to a complainant, and by following a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before the imposition of any disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures as defined in §106.30, against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment means complainants are offered supportive measures and respondents are afforded the §106.45 grievance process prior to disciplinary sanctions. Recipients must avoid favoritism and ensure procedures protect both parties' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of §106.45 grievance process to reach reliable factual determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of Title IX sexual harassment must be resolved through the §106.45 grievance process, designed to reach reliable factual determinations. Remedies (unlike supportive measures) and disciplinary sanctions should be tied to findings from that grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal grievance process is required before awarding remedies that would burden a respondent or imposing disciplinary sanctions. The process is designed to produce reliable outcomes even where evidence is scarce or recollections differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX personnel free from conflicts of interest and bias; impartial-training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Title IX Coordinator must be free from conflicts of interest and bias and, under revised §106.45(b)(1)(iii), trained in how to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment of the facts at issue. The Department added training that includes 'how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training materials must avoid sex stereotypes. The Department declines to prescribe exact training content (e.g., implicit bias training) but requires that training achieve the directive to teach impartial service and avoidance of prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias. This prohibition includes Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and persons who facilitate informal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation, including use of non-sexual conduct charges to punish reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Added §106.71 prohibiting retaliation against any individual exercising Title IX rights (including the right to refuse to participate in a grievance process). Charging an individual with a code of conduct violation that does not involve sexual harassment but arises out of the same facts or circumstances as sexual harassment allegations, for the purpose of interfering with rights under Title IX, constitutes retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaliation includes intimidation, threats, coercion, discrimination, or charging with code violations (e.g., charging a complainant for consensual sexual activity, underage drinking, or other conduct) when done to interfere with Title IX rights. The provision applies to complainants, respondents, and witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for disciplining materially false statements made in bad faith
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71(b)(2) provides that charging an individual with a code of conduct violation for making a materially false statement in bad faith in the course of a grievance proceeding does not constitute retaliation, but a determination regarding responsibility, alone, is not sufficient to conclude that any party made a materially false statement in bad faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may discipline a party for materially false statements made in bad faith, but they must not infer bad faith solely from the outcome of the case. The provision cautions against charging parties for falsehoods unless there is a specific finding of material falsity and bad faith beyond mere determination of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against inferring falsity from lack of responsibility finding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department cautions recipients to avoid concluding that allegations are 'false' based solely on the outcome of the case because lack of evidence sufficient to conclude responsibility does not necessarily imply that the allegations were unfounded or false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not state or imply that a complainant's allegations were false or in bad faith merely because a determination of non-responsibility was reached; doing so may constitute retaliation. Similarly, a determination of responsibility alone is insufficient to justify punishing a respondent for making a materially false statement in bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of anonymous and third-party (bystander) reporting and limits on response when parties unidentified
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised §106.8(a) and §106.30 to expressly state that third party (including 'bystander') reporting, as well as anonymous reporting (by the complainant or by a third party) is a permissible manner of triggering a recipient's response obligations. Irrespective of whether a report is anonymous, a recipient with actual knowledge must respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient cannot identify any of the parties involved based on an anonymous report, the appropriate response may differ and the recipient may not be able to offer supportive measures to an unknown complainant. Recipients should calibrate responses to what is 'not clearly unreasonable' under the known circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal discretion when respondent no longer enrolled/employed or evidence unobtainable
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(3)(ii) provides that if the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed by the recipient, or if specific circumstances prevent the recipient from gathering evidence sufficient to reach a determination as to the formal complaint or allegations therein, then the recipient has the discretion to dismiss the formal complaint or any allegations therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may dismiss formal complaints when they cannot gather sufficient evidence or when respondent status prevents adjudication; dismissal under these circumstances is discretionary and tied to the recipient's ability to reach a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary informal resolution processes (consent required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients also may choose to offer informal resolution processes as alternatives to a full investigation and adjudication of the formal complaint, with the voluntary consent of both the complainant and respondent, which may encourage some complainants to file a formal complaint where they may have been reluctant to do so if a full investigation and adjudication was the only option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution is permitted only with the voluntary consent of both parties and is subject to limits (e.g., not available for allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student). Facilitators of informal resolution must be free from conflicts of interest and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibility for effective implementation of remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a respondent is found responsible for sexual harassment as defined in §106.30, the recipient must provide remedies to the complainant designed to restore or preserve the complainant's equal access to education. The final regulations expressly require the Title IX Coordinator to be responsible for the effective implementation of remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies should be designed to restore or preserve equal access (distinct from supportive measures) and the Title IX Coordinator must ensure they are implemented effectively. Recipients should have processes to monitor and enforce remedy implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials must avoid sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of the training required under §106.45(b)(1)(iii) is left to the recipient's discretion so long as it achieves the provision's directive that such training provide instruction on how to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias, and that materials used in such training avoid sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department does not mandate specific modules (e.g., explicit implicit bias training), training must not perpetuate sex stereotypes and must instruct personnel on impartiality and avoidance of prejudgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect complainant autonomy in choosing how to proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department respects survivors' autonomy in deciding whether to initiate a grievance process in the higher education setting. A complainant may only want supportive measures, may wish to go through an informal process, or may want to file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should honor complainants' stated wishes regarding supportive measures, informal resolution, and filing formal complaints (subject to limited exceptions). The Title IX Coordinator's interactive discussion should center the complainant's preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a reasonably prompt timeframe to conclude grievance processes
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(v) requires recipients to have a reasonably prompt time frame for the conclusion of the grievance process, including any appeals or informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must set and adhere to reasonably prompt timelines for investigations, adjudications, appeals, and informal resolutions to ensure timely resolution while allowing due process.
